A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe BEAST and permit reliable comparison of text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. The title and formatting change, but the research identity is clear; the original Broader Impacts appendix moves from F to H.

before.justification: v1 reports original neural encoding, pose estimation and action segmentation experiments, including quantitative comparisons and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments across all three tasks and adds baseline comparisons, ablations, feature visualizations and computational measurements.

M1.justification: The adopted method retains ViT-B/16, masked reconstruction plus temporal InfoNCE, adjacent-frame positives, selected anchors, CLS projection and the downstream heads. Contrastive-only and alternative pooling variants are added as ablations. Revised loss-weight hyperparameters are experimental-setting changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three tasks using IBL, IBL-whisker, Facemap, Mirror-mouse, Mirror-fish, CRIM13 and CalMS21. Revised pretraining sample counts do not introduce new dataset, species or task coverage.

E2.justification: Neural encoding adds DINOv2, CLIP and VideoMAE comparisons (v2 Table 13). Pose estimation adds DINO, DINOv2, SAM and an evaluated DeepLabCut baseline (Figures 9 and 11); action segmentation adds DINOv2 (Table 15). Contrastive-only ViT-C comparisons are also introduced across the tasks.

E3.justification: Reported settings change substantially: Table 3 revises IBL pretraining from 138,600 to 270,025 frames and CalMS21 from 103,544 frames in 37 videos to 91,087 in 70 videos. Appendix B.3 changes contrastive-loss weights, and D.2 changes transformer pose-training learning rates from 0.001 to 0.00005. New experiments introduce matched DeepLabCut controls and A100 forward-pass benchmarking. These revisions do not establish which existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds contrastive-only loss ablations across downstream tasks, CLS-versus-mean-versus-attention pooling ablations (Table 7), anchor-frame UMAP inspection (Figure 6), patch-feature PCA visualizations (Figure 7), and computational-efficiency analysis (Table 8). Earlier frame-selection, sampling, augmentation and dimensionality analyses remain.

E5.justification: IBL reporting in Table 1 and the extended neural results changes from session-level variability to SEM over 842 neurons across five sessions; Figure 2 also revises its uncertainty display. Runtime measurements introduce mean and SD across 32 batches. Table 15 newly describes SD across five random train/validation splits, conflicting with the retained weight-initialization-seed description in E.3, so an actual resampling change is unresolved.

E6.justification: Numerous baseline, ablation and compute results are added, and existing neural scores and pose curves change. Table 1 changes zero-shot IBL BEAST from 0.337 to 0.292 BPS, while MAE-only IN+PT changes from 0.334 to 0.331, reversing their reported ordering. Revised settings and aggregation prevent interpreting this as a controlled performance decline. New Figure 9 identifies a DINOv2 advantage on Mirror-fish; most existing action-segmentation scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations of masked reconstruction, temporal InfoNCE and downstream models are retained. Notation is refined, but no substantive derivation, formal assumption, theorem or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contribution of a versatile experiment-specific backbone remain unchanged. The Introduction and Discussion add explicit superiority claims against foundation models such as DINOv2 and position BEAST as a computationally efficient alternative to native video models.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations of contrastive-only pose failures and interprets feature visualizations as evidence of finer spatial detail. The Discussion expands applicability qualifications for naturalistic environments, required sampling adaptations, interpretability, smaller-model tradeoffs and cross-dataset foundation models. Appendix D.3 acknowledges the new Mirror-fish exception, although broader superiority statements remain insufficiently qualified.

D1.justification: v2 replaces promises to release expanded IBL labels with explicit access instructions and supplies pretraining-frame archives, BEAST checkpoint access and licenses, and versioned code releases in a new Reproducibility Statement. It also documents temporal alignment/resampling, additional baseline checkpoints, computational benchmarking details and a practical workflow in Appendix G. These are documented resources; external availability was not checked.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially, including foundation models and additional pose-estimation systems. New Appendix F discusses pose-, image- and video-based animal SSL, adding works such as ContrastivePose, BAMS, Selfee and Animal-JEPA and explicitly distinguishing BEAST through its frame-based objectives and three-task evaluation. Several broader unsupervised-behavior citations from v1 are removed.

P1.justification: The title and front matter change, the Introduction is condensed, explanations are edited, and the Discussion is expanded. A Reproducibility Statement and two appendix sections are added. The main section sequence and original Appendices A-E retain their organization and much of their prose; most expansion accompanies new substantive content.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantial visual material: sampling and feature visualizations, two pose-comparison figures, and pooling and computational-efficiency tables. Figure 2 replaces session boxplots with uncertainty bars, Figure 3 adds contrastive-only curves and legend entries, and result tables expand. The conference format also changes page layout; several original diagrams and analyses are retained or relocated.

improvement.justification: Expanded comparisons, ablations and explicit model/data/code access strengthen evaluation and reproducibility. However, v2 retains a zero-shot superiority claim supported by v1 Table 1 but contradicted by v2 Table 1: BEAST scores 0.292 versus MAE-only's 0.331 on IBL. It also newly claims the combined loss beats MAE-only in action segmentation despite Table 15 retaining CalMS21 scores of 0.81 versus 0.82, and overstates consistency against pose baselines despite the Mirror-fish exception. These problems affect central scientific interpretations, leaving substantial benefits and material reporting harms without a reliably assessable net direction.
